hero.line2: Everything that actually moves the needle.
hero.intro: You do not need to pay for the knowledge to start an online career. Almost everything worth learning is already free — from the world's best universities, from the companies whose tools you'll use, from your own government, and from a few genuinely great teachers on YouTube. The hard part was never access. It's knowing which free thing is worth your week, and how to turn it into proof instead of a pile of half-finished tabs. That's what this page is for.
hero.creed: Free is only free if it doesn't cost you a month you can't get back. The skill isn't finding a course. It's judging one before it takes your time — and finishing it with something to show.

judge.title: How to judge any free course before it takes your week.
judge.lead: There is an ocean of free learning, and most of it is a comfortable way to feel productive without becoming more hireable. Run any course — including the ones we list below — through these five questions first. The ones worth your time survive all five.

tests.q: Does it end in a real artifact?
tests.why: A course you finish with nothing to show taught you nothing a client can see. Prefer the ones that make you build something — a project, a page, a working sheet — over the ones that just fill your head and hand you a certificate.

tests.q: Is it from the source, or a reseller?
tests.why: The vendor's or institution's own site — hubspot.com/academy, a real university on edX — is current, free, and correct. A stranger repackaging it on a course marketplace is usually neither free nor up to date. Go to the source.

AI and tools change every few months. A 2020 course on an AI product is a museum piece. Check when it was last updated before you trust a single click of it — especially for anything with 'AI' in the title.

tests.q: Free to audit, or free until the paywall?
tests.why: Plenty of 'free' courses gate the certificate, the exam, or the real lessons behind a trial that wants a card. Read the fine print for ninety seconds before you commit an afternoon, so the free part is actually the part you need.

tests.q: Does it teach the method or the buttons?
tests.why: A tutorial on where today's buttons are expires with the next redesign. The transferable method — why the tool exists, what it's really for — does not. Learn the version that survives the update.

judge.note: If a course fails these, it isn't bad — it's just not worth your scarce hours right now. Close the tab without guilt.

shelf.kicker: The shelf · go to the source
shelf.title: The free resources we actually point people to.
shelf.lead: Curated, not exhaustive — a shelf, not a warehouse. Each one is free or free-to-audit, from the source, and chosen because it ends in something you can use. Open the ones that fit your lane; ignore the rest. We link the primary site every time, so you always land on the real, current version.

groups.title: AI fluency — start here
groups.note: The single highest-leverage free study you can do this month. Learn to work with AI as a professional, not a tourist. Do the first one before anything else on this shelf.

groups.title: Philippine government & public — free by right
groups.note: Your taxes already paid for these. Free digital-skills training and certificates from Philippine public programs. Free is free — take the certificate, then go build the proof that actually gets you hired.

groups.title: Craft skills — from the people who made the tools
groups.note: The companies whose software you'll use, and the universities, give their courses away on purpose — a skilled user is a lifelong one. Pick the ones in your niche and finish with a project, not just a badge.

groups.title: YouTube — free teachers worth your time
groups.note: The best of YouTube rivals any paid course; the worst is a time sink dressed as learning. These channels are durable and genuinely teach a craft. Watch to build, not to binge.

protocol.title: Learning without proof is just entertainment.
protocol.lead: The mistake isn't picking the wrong course — it's finishing five of them and having nothing to show a client. A resource only counts once it turns into evidence. Run every item on this shelf through the same five moves.

steps.title: Pick one, tied to your niche
steps.desc: Not five. One resource, aimed at the exact outcome your chosen lane needs. Breadth feels productive and builds nothing; depth in one lane is what gets hired.

steps.title: Set the outcome before you start
steps.desc: Decide what you'll have built when you finish — a landing page, a reconciled sample ledger, a month of content — not "complete the course." A topic never ends; a deliverable does.

steps.title: Build as you go, not after
steps.desc: Pause the video and do the thing on your own file. Passive watching is the illusion of learning; the part where you're stuck is the part where it's actually happening.

steps.title: Collect proof, not certificates
steps.desc: A certificate is a receipt that says you attended. A portfolio piece is evidence that you can do the work. Clients hire the second one. Turn every course into a thing you can show.

steps.title: Use it on a real task fast
steps.desc: Put the new skill to work within a week — a micro-task, a free project for a cause you like, a rebuild from scratch. A skill you don't use within days is a skill you're about to forget.

closing.title: The paywall was never the thing standing between you and this career.
closing.body: Everything you need to start is on this shelf, for free, right now. What's scarce isn't the courses — it's the judgment to pick the right one, the discipline to finish it, and the habit of turning every hour of study into something a client can see. Those are free too. They just aren't easy, and that's exactly why the people who build them win.
closing.point: Start with one. Finish it with something built. Then come back for the next.
